1.why: Actionable reset tokens are issued only when the identifier matches the mock account, and verification consumes that token before binding recovery auth to the session.

2.why: A non-actionable decoy token cannot change the password, and an actionable token is single-use and not shared across users, so the same code does not work for any other user.

3.why: password-update clears only the current recovery authorization and never invalidates other entries in the sessions map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key and HSTS plus upgrade-insecure-requests are set, but the TLS protocol version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords use argon2id and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests, which is appropriate protection but not encryption of reset codes or user data.

6.why: There is no real email body; the API always returns the same generic message and does not include account identifiers, though a demo testToken is returned for simulation.

7.why: Identifiers, tokens, and passwords are validated with strict allowlists/rules, JSON bodies are type-checked, and the SPA inserts values only via textContent.

8.why: The only reset link built is a same-origin relative URL (/?reset=...), and the server has no open-redirect parameter handling.

9.why: No email HTML templates exist; simulated delivery does not interpolate user input into scripts or HTML.

10.why: Server error responses and the audit log avoid secrets, but the API returns testToken/testMfaCode and the on-page Logs UI prints recovery and MFA codes.

11.why: The live password is kept as an argon2id hash, yet MFA_TEST_CODE and the initial password plaintext are hardcoded in the source.

12.why: The fixed demo MFA code 246810 and known initial mock password act as default credentials that the flow accepts.

13.why: limited() throttles reset-request (3/10min), reset-verify (5/10min), and mfa-verify (5/10min) and returns 429 when exceeded.

14.why: reset-request always returns the same generic message and shape for every identifier, issuing decoy tokens for non-matches.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte base64url values from randomBytes, stored by SHA-256 digest, single-use/expiry-bound, and only the matching account gets an actionable token.
